domain_assessment.domain: Nuclear power plant emergency operating procedure revision and validation
domain_assessment.role: Procedure writer/engineer responsible for updating an Auxiliary Feedwater (AFW) Emergency Operating Procedure after an instrumentation design change
domain_assessment.objective: Produce an accurate, technically defensible, validated procedure revision before the outage implementation window
domain_assessment.incident_type: Time-pressured revision of an AFW procedure following replacement of a legacy analog level transmitter with a digital transmitter

decision_points.summary: The participant triages an external operating-experience report and begins incorporating it into the local draft before confirming whether the external transmitter is technically equivalent to the local unit.
evidence_before: An industry OE report described a transmitter failure involving a new digital level transmitter.
The local design change replaced a legacy analog level transmitter with a digital unit.
evidence_after: The I&C engineer explained that the OE equipment used a different sensing technology and vendor family.
The participant recognized that applicability was less direct than initially assumed.
goals_constraints: Rapidly identify relevant operating experience for the procedure revision.
Complete the revision within an approximately three-day window.
alternatives: Hold the OE report as provisionally low relevance pending equivalence confirmation.
Consult the I&C engineer before incorporating OE language.
Compare sensing technology and design characteristics before drafting.
decision_points.decision_basis: Surface match between the report framing, "new digital level transmitter failure," and the local equipment change.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate; the overall revision had a short three-day completion window, but no evidence indicates an immediate decision deadline at this moment.
decision_points.uncertainty: Technical equivalence between the OE transmitter and the local transmitter was not established before use.

decision_points.summary: The participant drafts verification steps using a familiar procedure-writing template and omits the new two-point calibration requirement.
evidence_before: The new digital transmitter required a two-point calibration check.
The old analog procedure did not require that check.
The participant had substantial prior experience writing AFW revisions.
evidence_after: Peer review identified that the calibration check was missing.
The participant acknowledged carrying forward the old pattern rather than rebuilding the section around the new requirement.
goals_constraints: Draft a usable verification section quickly.
Reconcile the procedure with the design change package.
alternatives: Build the verification section directly from the design-change requirements.
Consult the I&C engineer before drafting.
Perform requirement reconciliation before rather than after constructing the template-based structure.
decision_points.decision_basis: Reliance on a familiar and frequently used AFW procedure-writing sequence.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate; the revision remained subject to the outage deadline.
decision_points.uncertainty: The participant had the design package available but deferred a requirement-specific reconciliation.

decision_points.summary: The participant selects a recent but less relevant test as the basis for validation criteria instead of systematically comparing it with five years of historical surveillance data.
evidence_before: Five years of AFW surveillance history were available.
A two-week-old test from an unrelated procedure used a similar-looking verification form.
evidence_after: A fuller data pull showed that older tests contained operating conditions more closely aligned with the transmitter's actual fault signature.
goals_constraints: Set validation criteria for confirming that the revised procedure steps work as intended.
Use a practical benchmark under schedule constraints.
alternatives: Systematically compare the recent test against older surveillance results for fault-mode relevance.
Prioritize historical cases with matching operating conditions.
Use multiple tests rather than a single proxy.
decision_points.decision_basis: The two-week-old test was top of mind and appeared to be a reasonable proxy because the form looked similar.
decision_points.time_pressure: Moderate; the task occurred within the same constrained revision schedule.
decision_points.uncertainty: The participant did not determine comparative relevance to the local transmitter's fault modes before weighting the recent test.

decision_points.summary: With less than 24 hours remaining, the participant terminates further information gathering after reviewing accessible records and makes a final residual-risk judgment through a mental failure-mode review before submitting the draft.
evidence_before: Part of the OE database was inaccessible due to a concurrent audit.
The participant had access to a control-room log and personal notes.
The participant could have sought an extension or escalated to the Shift Technical Advisor.
The procedure still required final risk assessment before board submission.
evidence_after: The approval board requested a supplemental risk note because the draft did not address a failure mode.
The participant later stated that their confidence had exceeded what the evidence supported.
goals_constraints: Submit before the outage implementation window.
Determine whether residual risk was acceptable despite incomplete OE access.
alternatives: Request more time or an extension to access and review fuller OE records.
Escalate the unresolved question to the Shift Technical Advisor.
Delay submission pending a complete transmitter-model OE search.
Use a structured failure-mode-by-failure-mode review rather than recall-based mental synthesis.
decision_points.decision_basis: Accessible records felt sufficient; the participant recalled failure modes from the design package, judged major ones covered, and accepted residual risk.
decision_points.time_pressure: High; the deadline was under 24 hours away and the participant perceived an extension as disruptive to outage planning.
decision_points.uncertainty: The complete OE record and complete transmitter-specific failure-mode inventory were unavailable or not reviewed.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “‘New digital level transmitter failure’ matched our situation closely enough that it registered as the same kind of event. I didn't stop to verify the sensing technology before I started drafting around it.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: OE-report discussion, participant response after the interviewer asks what specifically made the report seem applicable.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant treated surface resemblance in equipment category and event framing as sufficient evidence of applicability, before checking the technically discriminative feature: sensing technology and vendor family.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: The participant may initially have made a reasonable preliminary relevance triage under time pressure. However, the text explicitly shows that drafting began before equivalence was checked and that technical non-equivalence was subsequently discovered.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The interview identifies the initial cue, omitted verification step, subsequent disconfirming evidence, and the affected drafting action.

revision.location: Decision point 1, initial OE-report triage and subsequent probe.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the current sequence: surface match, no equivalence check, I&C correction, and participant acknowledgment.
preserve: The distinction between general equipment labels and sensing-technology equivalence.
The fact that this occurs only during OE applicability triage.
avoid_creating: A second similarity-based applicability judgment at another decision point.
Explicit use of the label "Similarity Bias" in dialogue.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I've written a lot of these AFW revisions over the years, so I built the verification section using the template sequence I normally use.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Procedure-drafting account and follow-up question regarding sources relied on during drafting.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: A well-practiced, frequently deployed procedure-writing sequence intruded into a changed task context, causing the participant to construct the section from the legacy pattern before reconciling it with the digital transmitter's specific calibration requirement.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Templates can be an efficient and appropriate drafting aid. The bias mechanism is supported here because the participant describes using the familiar structure first, deferring reconciliation, and missing a novel requirement that the template did not contain.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The interview links repeated prior practice, automatic template use, the novel requirement, and the omission.

revision.location: Decision point 2, verification-step drafting and source-reliance probe.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Keep the contrast between the habitual template sequence and the design-package-specific two-point calibration requirement.
preserve: The participant's prior AFW procedure-writing experience.
The distinct action-selection operation of drafting.
Peer review as the source that reveals the omission.
avoid_creating: Reframing ordinary use of a template as automatically biased without retaining the requirement-specific omission.
Adding another habit-based episode during final submission.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “That one was fresh in my head, so I anchored the validation criteria around it.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Validation-criteria discussion and follow-up question on how historical data were weighted.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The most recently encountered test was disproportionately used as the representative baseline because it was cognitively available, despite older surveillance tests containing operating conditions more relevant to the transmitter's fault signature.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Recent data may sometimes be substantively preferable. Here, however, the participant identifies recency and form similarity rather than transmitter-fault relevance as the basis for selection, while later evidence establishes that older data were more relevant.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The text supplies the temporal cue, the weighting decision, the unperformed comparison, and the later relevance contrast.

revision.location: Decision point 3, selection of surveillance-test benchmark.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain both the explicit top-of-mind cue and the later finding that older tests better represented the relevant operating conditions.
preserve: The distinction between recency and technical relevance.
avoid_creating: A second availability or recency episode in the final failure-mode review.
An implication that all newer data are inherently less valid.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I looked at what was actually accessible — the control room log, my notes — and it felt like enough to call it done. The audit had the fuller OE records locked up, and requesting an extension felt like it would just push the whole outage schedule, so I didn't pursue that.”
target_occurrence_audit.evidence_location: Final-stretch account and follow-up question on readiness to submit.
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The participant adopts a satisficing stopping rule: once readily accessible records appear minimally sufficient, information search ends despite recognized incompleteness and available escalation or schedule-management alternatives.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Limited access and an impending outage deadline are real operational constraints, so a bounded search can be rational. The occurrence remains supported because the participant did not merely lack access; they judged partial materials sufficient, declined to pursue an extension, and declined escalation despite an acknowledged unresolved question.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: No revision is necessary, although the present evidence supports a constrained satisficing interpretation rather than an unequivocally irrational one.

revision.location: Decision point 4, information-gathering termination before final submission.
revision.current_defect: None material; the constraint-sensitive interpretation should be retained.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Keep the separation between ending the search based on accessible records and the later mental synthesis of residual risk.
preserve: The locked OE database and outage-deadline constraints.
The unpursued extension and unpursued Shift Technical Advisor escalation.
The control-room log and personal notes as the evidence source for this occurrence.
avoid_creating: Portraying the database lock itself as a bias.
Collapsing search termination into the later risk-acceptability judgment.
Adding an unsupported claim that exhaustive search was operationally required.

target_occurrence_audit.supporting_quote: “I did a mental run-through of the failure modes and figured we'd covered the main ones.”
target_occurrence_audit.mechanism: The final risk-acceptability judgment is synthesized through a recall-based, simplified holistic estimate rather than a structured review of the complete transmitter-specific failure-mode set. The participant later recognizes that their confidence exceeded the available evidence.
target_occurrence_audit.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Experienced practitioners can appropriately use mental simulation under time pressure, and a poor outcome alone would not establish flawed reasoning. Support is sufficient here because the mental review followed incomplete OE access, relied on recalled rather than fully cross-checked failure modes, omitted a failure mode, and was later described as more confident than the evidence warranted.
target_occurrence_audit.additional_evidence_needed: None. The account differentiates this final synthesis from the preceding decision to stop searching for information.

revision.location: Decision point 4, final residual-risk synthesis immediately before approval-board submission.
revision.minimal_change_instruction: Retain the recall-based mental failure-mode review, the final risk-acceptability call, and the later calibration statement about confidence exceeding evidence.
preserve: The temporal order: search termination first, final risk synthesis second.
The incomplete failure-mode documentation as the distinct evidence source.
The participant's qualified rather than categorical confidence.
avoid_creating: A duplicate bounded-rationality occurrence by focusing again on inaccessible records.
An explicit claim that any mental simulation is inherently biased.
A second final-judgment episode elsewhere in the interview.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “Now, knowing the board found a gap, I'd say I was more confident than the evidence actually supported.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The participant retrospectively identifies a mismatch between confidence in residual-risk acceptability and the amount and completeness of available evidence.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: This statement may be appropriate retrospective recalibration after receiving new information from the approval board, rather than independent evidence that the participant exhibited a distinct overconfidence bias at the time. It also functions as supporting context for the planned imperfect-rationality occurrence.

additional_candidate_biases.supporting_quote: “I ran through the failure modes I could recall from the design package.”
additional_candidate_biases.mechanism: The final review used readily recalled failure modes rather than a complete documented list.
additional_candidate_biases.plausible_nonbias_explanation: Recall-based review may be a practical consequence of the unavailable OE database and limited time, and the text does not establish that easily recalled failure modes were affirmatively treated as more probable or representative. This evidence is better retained as part of the intended imperfect-rationality mechanism.

nonbias_cues.cue: The three-day revision window and the impending outage implementation deadline.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Time pressure is an operational constraint. It provides context for the decisions but does not, by itself, show a biased reasoning mechanism.

nonbias_cues.cue: The OE database was partly locked due to a concurrent audit.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Restricted access is missing information or an organizational constraint, not a cognitive bias. The relevant reasoning evidence is the participant's decision to stop searching and accept available records as sufficient.

nonbias_cues.cue: Peer review found the missing calibration check.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Peer-review detection is a procedural control and outcome. The habit-intrusion occurrence is supported by the participant's template-first drafting process, not simply by the reviewer finding an error.

nonbias_cues.cue: The approval board later requested a supplemental risk note.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: An unfavorable downstream outcome does not independently demonstrate bias. It corroborates the importance of examining the prior reasoning but is not the basis for classification.

nonbias_cues.cue: The participant considered, but did not use, I&C consultation and Shift Technical Advisor escalation.
nonbias_cues.why_not_bias: Failure to consult a colleague is not intrinsically biased. It becomes relevant only where the text specifies the operative mechanism: surface similarity, habitual templating, or satisficing under constraints.

causal_claims.claim: Initial OE-report applicability was weakened because the external transmitter used different sensing technology and a different vendor family.
causal_claims.support: The I&C engineer identifies the technical mismatch after the participant has begun drafting from the report.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported as a causal explanation for why the original applicability inference was unreliable, though the interview does not establish how the inappropriate OE language affected the final procedure.

causal_claims.claim: Template-first drafting contributed to omission of the two-point calibration check.
causal_claims.support: The participant states that they built the normal template structure first, deferred reconciliation to the design package, and peer review found the missing new requirement.

causal_claims.claim: Recency-based weighting produced a less relevant validation benchmark.
causal_claims.support: The participant chose the two-week-old test because it was fresh in mind; subsequent review identified older data with closer operating-condition relevance.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported. The interview establishes a mismatch in relevance, but does not quantify whether the selected benchmark materially changed the ultimate validation conclusion.

causal_claims.claim: Partial OE review and a recall-based final review contributed to an unaddressed failure mode.
causal_claims.support: The participant submitted after reviewing accessible records and mentally reviewing recalled failure modes; the approval board subsequently identified a missing failure mode.
causal_claims.assessment: Moderately supported but not conclusive. The omitted failure mode could also have been absent for technical, documentation, or review-process reasons not explored in the interview.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Treating the approval board's later supplemental-risk request as proof that the participant's final reasoning was biased.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: Classify the reasoning from the participant's stated search termination, recall-based synthesis, and confidence calibration; use the board outcome only as corroborative context.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Treating the fact that older surveillance tests were more relevant as proof that choosing a newer test was irrational.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: The defensible mechanism is disproportionate weighting from recency without a systematic relevance comparison, not merely selection of a recent datum.

correlation_causation_risks.risk: Treating restricted database access as evidence of a cognitive failure.
correlation_causation_risks.mitigation: Separate the external constraint from the participant's satisficing decision and unpursued alternatives.

causal_audit.changed_variable: Not applicable; the interview includes reflective hypotheticals about additional time and database access, but no designed causal counterfactual condition.
causal_audit.explanation: The narrative has coherent temporal links between reasoning episodes and later corrective information. It appropriately contains natural retrospective hypotheticals, but those statements are not controlled counterfactual evidence and should not be treated as demonstrating what would certainly have occurred under different conditions.

global_revision_constraints: Do not treat the schedule, unavailable OE database, peer-review finding, or approval-board outcome as stand-alone bias evidence.
Maintain the distinction at decision point 4 between information-search termination and final risk-acceptability synthesis.
Do not introduce explicit bias terminology into the participant's dialogue.
Do not add a second episode of any target bias while preserving the current narrative.
